subject: Post-demo: evaluation plan & targeted parity tests vs hyperscalers
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Evan Cole <evan.cole@averytech.com>; Maya Singh <maya.singh@averytech.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: evaluation plan & targeted parity tests vs hyperscalers

Hi Evan / Maya —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Appreciate the candid feedback on where you need parity with your current hyperscaler endpoints. Per the conversation, I captured a short plan below so we can move quickly on a hands-on comparison.

Quick recap (what you asked for):
- Confirm Redwood parity on: tool/function-calling reliability, structured JSON outputs, and streaming latency/ordering under concurrent sessions.
- Measure cost/token and p99 latency for your typical 1–2k token flows.
- Validate fallback behavior for short outages (model variant + routing).

Proposed concrete next steps (we can start as early as next week):
1) Run three focused tests (we'll provide the harness):
   - Function calling correctness: 1000 scripted calls using your top-10 function schemas (check for missing/extra args and malformed JSON).
   - Structured output conformity: 500 prompts across 5 schemas; validate strict JSON vs relaxed parsing (we'll attach an evaluation matrix).
   - Streaming stress: 200 concurrent streams with typical 1–2k tokens; measure p50/p95/p99 and ordering under bursts.
2) Provide a side-by-side report vs your current provider (we'll run equivalent runs against a compatible open model on Redwood and collect the metrics).
3) Joint sync after tests (30 min) to review regressions and next actions (canary, pricing).

Logistics I need from you to schedule runs:
- A sample of the 10 function schemas (or a single representative set) — spreadsheet attached as av_test_plan.xlsx.
- Two structured-output examples per schema (we can accept relaxed examples).
- Preferred window for stress test (UTC ranges are fine).

I'll loop in Rishi for measurement/infra leads and Aditya for runtime/compat questions. If this looks good I'll schedule the first test run and share an eval matrix doc with pass/fail criteria.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0196

Attachments: av_test_plan.xlsx (spreadsheet with function schemas)

From: Evan Cole <evan.cole@averytech.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@averytech.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: evaluation plan & targeted parity tests vs hyperscalers

Monica —

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A few clarifying points from our side before you spin up runs: 

1) Function calling: we have a strict signature for our order fulfillment function (order.submit). We will share the exact JSON schema; the primary concern is ensuring no silent coercion and predictable error codes for missing required fields.

2) Streaming: Our sessions often interleave tool calls mid-stream (e.g., user prompt -> tool call -> resume stream). Can you confirm Redwood preserves event ordering and provides mid-stream tool call markers?

3) Side-by-side: We need the same prompt seeds and request metadata (temperature, top_p, max_tokens) so the comparisons are apples-to-apples.

We're good to run the function-calling and structured-output tests next Tue/Wed (UTC windows 14:00–18:00). Stress streaming test we prefer Fri 10:00–14:00 UTC to align with our load window.

I'll attach the order.submit schema and two structured-output examples in a separate email.

—Evan
Evan Cole
Platform Engineering Manager | AveryTech
evanc@averytech.com

Monica — forwarding Evan's confirmation and notes.

Our immediate checklist for infra: 
- Ensure deterministic function-calling logs (request/response + structured args) are retained and exportable.
- Add explicit mid-stream markers in the stream payload (we already support opaque 'event' frames; make sure we expose docs so Avery can validate ordering).
- Prepare a paired run against their hyperscaler baseline (we can use their prompt seeds + same sampling params).

QA item: when they say "no silent coercion" — we should run a strict JSON validator as part of the function-calling harness and flag any auto-corrections. Aditya, can your team add a strict mode to the harness to fail on coercion?

Rishi
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Evan / Maya —

Perfect — thanks for the windows. We've scheduled the initial runs as follows and attached our evaluation matrix (redwood-eval-matrix.md) with pass/fail criteria and measurement hooks: 

- Function calling (strict mode): Tue 24 Mar 2026 14:00–16:00 UTC
- Structured output validation: Wed 25 Mar 2026 14:00–16:00 UTC
- Streaming stress + mid-stream events: Fri 27 Mar 2026 10:00–13:00 UTC

What we'll need from Avery before Tue: the order.submit schema and any rejection codes you consider critical to surface. If you can drop those by EOD Monday (or link the Drive folder) we'll ingest them into the harness.

Post-run deliverables (what you'll get):
- Raw logs (request/response + event markers) and an anonymized side-by-side latency/cost table.
- A list of any behavioral diffs (e.g., JSON coercions, missing fields, stream reordering) with reproduction seeds.
- Recommended mitigations: runtime flags (strict mode), fallback routing config, and if needed a canary rollout plan.

If all looks good I can send calendar invites and a shared Drive folder. Thanks again — looking forward to the runs.

Best,
Monica

Attachments: redwood-eval-matrix.md (evaluation matrix + acceptance criteria)
